Support Industry.text: Behind every pro hero stands the support industry. Support companies design and manufacture hero costumes, protective gear, tools and devices, each built around a specific Quirk and body: heat-resistant fabrics for fire users, gauntlets that store or channel a Quirk's output, goggles, capture weapons, breathing gear, grappling lines and armor. A large company may outfit dozens of agencies, while small workshops live on custom pieces. Hero gear is regulated. Equipment used in the field must meet government standards and be registered, and selling unregistered support gear, especially weapons, is a crime, though brokers trade it anyway. Hero Course students at U.A. Academy submit costume designs with their applications; the academy passes them to contracted support companies, which deliver working costumes for the start of hero training, and students revise them as their Quirks and techniques develop. Designers learn the trade in support courses at hero academies and engineering schools. At U.A. the Support Course trains them in the Development Studio under Power Loader, where students build, test and occasionally blow up prototypes, and the best pitch their work to companies at public events. Good support design starts from what a hero actually needs and respects what a body can take. Gear that covers a weakness is prized; gear that hides a weakness the wearer has not learned to manage is dangerous.
